kinds.summary: A depletion run's time steps, power or flux normalisation, k at each step, per-material nuclide densities and provenance, on a heavy-metal basis.
kinds.manual: In OpenMC Studio, run a depletion (the Reactor Physics package; it needs the depletion chain file) and save its depletion record, a studio.depletion JSON written next to the statepoint. Give that file to the app that asks for it.

kinds.summary: A D-T neutron source of a tokamak design point: poloidal cells with rate in neutrons per second, ion temperature and energy spread, the plasma boundary, and the total rate that turns a per-source-particle tally into a per-second one.
kinds.manual: In PLOW, open the design point and run `python -m plow records point.json --out-dir out` (or the Records tab in the editor). The file out/<name>.fusion-source.json is the record. To make one by hand, write the JSON described in docs/records.md of the PLOW repository: the cells need r_m, z_m, volume_m3, rate_n_s, ti_kev and energy_std_mev. It is an educational result, not validated for design, safety or licensing use.

kinds.summary: The first-wall contour of a tokamak design point in the poloidal plane: a counter-clockwise polygon in R and Z, and for each segment its midpoint, length, outward normal and area as a band of revolution.
kinds.manual: In PLOW, run `python -m plow records point.json --out-dir out`. The file out/<name>.first-wall-geometry.json is the record. By hand: list the wall polygon in metres (R, Z, counter-clockwise) and give each segment's length, normal and area 2 pi R_mid L, as described in docs/records.md of the PLOW repository. It is an educational result, not validated for design, safety or licensing use.

kinds.summary: The heat flux on each first-wall segment of a tokamak design point in MW per square metre: direct 14 MeV neutron wall load by line of sight, core radiation, and their sum with a blanket energy multiplication. Names the hashes of the two records it came from.
kinds.manual: In PLOW, run `python -m plow records point.json --out-dir out`. The file out/<name>.blanket-heat-load.json is the record. It needs the fusion-source and first-wall-geometry records first: the wall load comes from them. Hand-made records must carry their SHA-256 hashes, see docs/records.md of the PLOW repository. It is an educational result, not validated for design, safety or licensing use.
